title: Model-Visible Representation Taxonomy for Multimodal Biological Foundation Models
classification_unit: one input route: a single source object carried through its transformation chain to the form visible to the generative multimodal model
organizing_principle: Partition routes by the model-visible carrier mechanism, not by paper, task, or source modality. Source modality, lifecycle phase, text role, and fusion topology are treated as orthogonal dimensions so that actual inputs, training-only targets, generated outputs, baselines, and ablations remain distinguishable without forcing them into a single catch-all bucket.

families.name: Text-native token streams
families.definition: Routes whose model-visible form is a text-token sequence: free-form prompts, structured prompts with biological slots, serialized cell or gene sentences, or multi-instance textual context. The biologic content is carried by language tokens rather than dense vectors, images, or geometric states.
families.structural_criterion: The generative backbone receives ordinary text tokens, even when the content is biologically specialized or templated.

leaves.name: Free-form prompt or question
leaves.definition: A natural-language prompt, question, or instruction that reaches the model as ordinary text without a dedicated biological slot syntax.
include_when: The visible carrier is a plain text question, instruction, or conversational turn.
The route does not require a specialized biological serializer before model intake.
exclude_when: The route is primarily a slot-filled biological template or metadata schema.
The route is a sentence-like serialization of cells, genes, or ranked biological entities.
The model-visible carrier is dense embeddings, images, or diffusion states.

leaves.name: Structured biological prompt
leaves.definition: A text prompt that encodes explicit biological slots, metadata fields, or slot-filling task definitions such as gene, chromosome, indication, perturbation, or variant identifiers.
include_when: The text contains explicit biological fields or templated slots.
The prompt is designed to carry structured context, not just free-form question answering.
exclude_when: The input is only a plain conversational question.
The route is a sentence-like serialization of cells or genes rather than a slot schema.
The visible carrier is a dense embedding or an image.

leaves.name: Serialized biological context or sentence
leaves.definition: A text-token sequence produced by serializing cells, genes, ranked gene lists, neighborhoods, or multi-cell contexts into language-like sentences or ordered lists before model intake.
include_when: The route converts biological objects into cell sentences, gene sentences, ranked gene lists, or comparable serialized text.
The visible carrier is a textual summary of biological context, often across multiple nearby entities or samples.
exclude_when: The route is a simple question or instruction with no biological serialization.
The route is a fixed slot template with explicit metadata fields rather than a serialized biological narrative.
The visible carrier is a dense vector, image, or diffusion state.

families.name: Dense continuous carriers
families.definition: Routes whose model-visible form is a learned dense vector, soft-token block, prefix embedding, resampled latent, or similar continuous carrier inserted into a generative backbone. The biological source is encoded rather than discretely tokenized.
families.structural_criterion: The source is converted into continuous embeddings, soft tokens, or learned latent blocks before reaching the generator.

leaves.name: Direct projected embedding
leaves.definition: A continuous embedding projected from a biological encoder into the language or multimodal backbone, typically via a linear layer, connector, or latent-space projector.
include_when: The route explicitly projects biological inputs into an embedding space or unified latent space.
The visible carrier is a dense vector block rather than text tokens or image patches.
exclude_when: The carrier is a fixed prompt prefix of virtual tokens rather than direct projection.
The carrier is an image patch sequence or a discrete biological token stream.
The carrier is a diffusion state or geometric constraint.

leaves.name: Virtual-token prefix
leaves.definition: A fixed-length block of learned virtual tokens or multimodal prefix tokens that stands in for the biological source before being concatenated or inserted into the language backbone.
include_when: The route uses a fixed prefix, virtual token block, or multimodal prefix.
The biological source is not passed as ordinary text but as a learned prefix-like embedding bundle.
exclude_when: The route uses direct projection into a latent space without a dedicated prefix block.
The carrier is a single pooled embedding, an image patch set, or a diffusion state.

leaves.name: Cross-attention, resampler, or adapter-mediated embedding
leaves.definition: A dense carrier that reaches the backbone through a learned connector such as cross-attention, a resampler, a query-former, or an adapter layer.
include_when: The route explicitly uses cross-attention, a query-former, a resampler, or an adapter.
The biological content is converted to dense tokens before fusion with the backbone.
exclude_when: The route is a fixed virtual-token prefix.
The route is a direct embedding projection without a separate mediator.
The route is a raw image or a discrete biological token stream.

leaves.name: Pooled or aggregated embeddings
leaves.definition: A continuous carrier formed by aggregating multiple inputs into one embedding before model intake, such as averaging selected-cell embeddings or similar pooling operations.
include_when: The route compresses multiple biological items into one embedding before downstream use.
The visible form is a pooled representation rather than a single-source projection.
exclude_when: The route keeps separate tokens for each instance in the prompt.
The route uses raw images, discrete tokens, or a diffusion state.

families.name: Discrete biological symbol streams
families.definition: Routes whose biological source is represented as a discrete token stream native to or added to the tokenizer, rather than as text prose or dense embeddings. This includes biological BPE streams and multi-track structural token systems.
families.structural_criterion: The model-visible carrier is a tokenized biological sequence or structured biological symbol stream.

leaves.name: Tokenized biological corpus stream
leaves.definition: A biological sequence corpus tokenized into model-visible tokens, typically with an extended tokenizer or chunking protocol.
include_when: The route uses tokenized DNA, RNA, protein, or comparable sequence corpora.
The visible form is a chunked biological token stream rather than a prompt or embedding.
exclude_when: The route is an ordinary text prompt or instruction.
The route is a dense embedding prefix or image patch input.

leaves.name: Multi-track structural token stream
leaves.definition: A token stream that explicitly preserves multiple structural tracks or aligned symbol alphabets, such as sequence plus secondary-structure or tertiary-structure tracks.
include_when: The route preserves several aligned structural tracks in one discrete token stream.
The visible carrier is a structured symbolic alphabet, not an embedding.
exclude_when: The route is a single-track tokenized corpus.
The route is a continuous prefix, image patch, or diffusion state.

families.name: Visual and raster carriers
families.definition: Routes whose model-visible form is an image, patch grid, slide tile, or other rasterized visual carrier processed by a vision encoder or equivalent visual front end.
families.structural_criterion: The source is presented as pixels, patches, or visual tokens rather than language tokens or dense embeddings alone.

leaves.name: Raw slide or patch input
leaves.definition: A histology or similar biomedical image presented directly as a raster image, patch, or patch set to a vision encoder.
include_when: The route starts from a raw image patch or whole-slide image.
The visible carrier is an image tensor or patch grid.
exclude_when: The route is a projected embedding or text prompt.
The route is a diffusion state or discrete biological token stream.

leaves.name: Patch-context or case-level visual reasoning
leaves.definition: A visual route where multiple patches or registered sections are combined into a case-level image context before prediction or reasoning.
include_when: The route uses neighboring patches, serial sections, or case-level visual context.
The visible carrier is still visual, but the unit is a patch set or contextualized slide view.
exclude_when: The route uses only a single raw patch without contextual aggregation.
The route is text-only or embedding-only.

families.name: Geometric and diffusion-state carriers
families.definition: Routes whose model-visible form is a geometric constraint, coordinate state, or noisy latent state used by a diffusion or structure-generation model. These routes are structurally distinct from ordinary embeddings because the carrier is organized by geometry or diffusion time.
families.structural_criterion: The model-visible carrier is a coordinate/constraint object or a time-indexed noisy latent state rather than a token sequence or patch grid.

leaves.name: Noisy diffusion state
leaves.definition: A time-indexed noisy latent state or training state used directly in a diffusion process.
include_when: The route exposes noisy coordinates or another diffusion-time latent state to the model.
The carrier is part of forward or reverse diffusion dynamics.
exclude_when: The route is a static coordinate constraint or a text prompt.
The route is an image, token stream, or dense embedding prefix.

leaves.name: Coordinate or backbone conditioning
leaves.definition: A geometric conditioning route in which the model receives coordinates, substructures, or point-cloud-derived geometry as the visible carrier.
include_when: The route conditions on backbone coordinates, substructures, or point clouds.
The model-visible form is geometric rather than textual.
exclude_when: The route is an abstract symbolic label or a free-text prompt.
The route is a noisy diffusion state rather than a stable geometric condition.

leaves.name: Symbolic structural constraint
leaves.definition: A non-textual or lightly symbolic structural condition such as symmetry, class labels, or other geometry-level control signals supplied to the generator.
include_when: The route conditions generation with symbolic structural labels or abstract geometry constraints.
The carrier is a constraint signal rather than a language prompt or a dense embedding.
exclude_when: The route is a free-form natural-language caption or question.
The route is a coordinate/backbone carrier or noisy diffusion state.

orthogonal_dimensions.name: Biological modality
orthogonal_dimensions.definition: The underlying biological source domain of the route, treated separately from the carrier mechanism because the same modality can be serialized, embedded, rasterized, or diffused.

orthogonal_dimensions.name: Lifecycle phase
orthogonal_dimensions.definition: The training or evaluation stage at which the route is used. This dimension prevents training-only targets, generated outputs, baselines, and inference inputs from being conflated.

orthogonal_dimensions.name: Text role / route status
orthogonal_dimensions.definition: The role played by text or symbolic material in the route, including whether it is an actual model input, a paired training input, a target, or a baseline/auxiliary prompt.

orthogonal_dimensions.name: Fusion topology
orthogonal_dimensions.definition: How the carrier is inserted into or combined with the generative backbone. This is orthogonal to the carrier type itself.

orthogonal_dimensions.name: Source-to-carrier transformation
orthogonal_dimensions.definition: The dominant transformation applied to the source object before it becomes model-visible. This captures whether the route is serialized, tokenized, projected, rasterized, aggregated, or driven by diffusion.

category_errors_prevented: Collapsing free-form text prompts, serialized biological sentences, and dense embeddings into one broad multimodal bucket.
Treating biological sequence tokenization as if it were ordinary prose.
Treating images or slide patches as if they were just another embedding prefix.
Treating diffusion-time noisy states as if they were static coordinate embeddings.
Folding training-only targets, generated outputs, baselines, and ablations into the same class as actual model inputs.
Using source modality as the primary axis when the visible carrier mechanism is the relevant structural criterion.
unresolved_questions: Some caption- or label-conditioned Chroma routes sit near the boundary between text-native conditioning and structural constraint conditioning; the current hierarchy keeps the carrier mechanism first and uses the orthogonal status dimensions to separate them.

Several multimodal papers describe a connector or projector without fully specifying the pre-encoder representation for all modalities; those routes are grouped by the visible carrier that is actually stated in the inventory.
Future corpora may justify splitting serialized biological sentences from general prompt text more finely if a dedicated symbolic syntax becomes common enough to function as its own carrier class.
